Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back! The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. Shadman Islam and Zakir Hasan will open the innings for Bangladesh. Mir Hamza will start with the new ball for Pakistan. Away we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Bangladesh's openers have a tricky phase to negotiate before the close of play. As per our estimation, they'll have 5 minutes to contend with, which should account for a couple of overs. We'll be back shortly for the start of Bangladesh's reply.

Pakistan end up with 274 on the board! Given the way they dominated the first session, they will be disappointed with this total. Five out of their top six batters got starts, but only Shan Masood and Saim Ayub managed to convert those into fifties. That said, it could have been a lot worse for them if not for Agha Salman's resilient knock. He batted with the tail, even though he had his fair share of chances as Bangladesh's bowlers continued to apply pressure throughout the day. Bangladesh would have taken this total at the start of the day. Mehidy Hasan led the charge with a five-wicket haul while Taskin Ahmed chipped in with three wickets.

OUT! STUMPED! It's all over! Mehidy Hasan gets his FIFTH wicket as he gets rid of Abrar Ahmed. Floats the ball away from the batter outside the off stump and Abrar Ahmed dances down the track for a big shot. The batter misses the ball completely and Litton Das does the rest behind the stumps. Pakistan are bowled out for 274 runs in the first innings of the match.

Commentary.Commentary: And we are back after Tea for the final session of the day. Pakistan lost 4 wickets in the second session and are currently 183/5 as the players and the umpires walk out to the field for the final session. Mohammad Rizwan and Agha Salman are the batters for Pakistan and it's Shakib Al Hasan who will start off the session with the ball in hand. Let's play!
... DAY 2, FINAL SESSION ...

Right then, with Bangladesh having a slight upper hand at the moment, Pakistan will aim to come out stronger after the break and their main goal would be to see through the day without losing many wickets. Bangladesh would try to sustain the pressure and chip in with quick wickets to restrict the hosts to a sub-par total. Stay tuned as the final session of Day 2 will begin at 10.15 am GMT.

Post-lunch, Bangladesh's bowling attack looked in discipline. The pitch offered some assistance, with the ball skidding off the surface initially and challenging the batter's technique. Nahid Rana and Mehidy Hasan emerged as a potent duo in tandem, relentlessly probing and maintaining pressure. It was Mehidy Hasan who ultimately broke through for Bangladesh, first dismantling the frustrating 107-run stand, and then following up with the crucial wicket of Saim Ayub in quick succession. Fresh off their spells, Taskin Ahmed and Shakib too chipped in with a wicket each which caused the visitors to weigh heavier on the hosts.

Babar Azam, in search of runs to his name, began his innings with purposeful intent, seeking to create the momentum. However, Pakistan's position became a bit more challenging as Saud Shakeel failed to capitalize on his earlier reprieve. But overall, throughout the session, an undercurrent of tension ran through. Furthering their trouble, just at the cusp of Tea break, Babar Azam fell at the most inopportune time.

The second session, typically prime time for batters to flourish, took a turn against Pakistan. Just a couple of overs in, they suffered an early setback as the composed Shan Masood fell for a well-crafted 57, despite looking comfortable at the crease. The blow was quickly compounded when Saim Ayub, fresh off his half-century, also fell in rapid succession. With two well-settled batters back in the dugout and with two new batters in the middle, it forced Pakistan to regroup and rebuild once more.

TEA, DAY 2 - SESSION SUMMARY - 30 overs, 84 runs, 4 wickets. This brings us to the end of the second session and Bangladesh would be mighty pleased with their collective disciplined bowling efforts. After just a solitary wicket in the first session, the visitors marched on strongly and kept Pakistan on their toes taking timely wickets. Whereas, Pakistani batters, despite getting starts, couldn't extend their innings and it led to a mini-collapse which reads Pakistan slipping from 107/1 at the start of the session to a worrisome 183/5.

This has been a good little phase for Bangladesh as they have managed to send back both the well-settled batters, Shan Masood and Saim Ayub back to the pavilion in a quick interval. With Babar and Shakeel in the middle now, Pakistan would want to see this session through without any further loss of wickets. The first session gave us really good cricket from the Pakistan batters and a lot of work needs to be done here on for the Bangladeshi bowlers. Let’s see what pans out in the second session of the game as we come back for the post-Lunch session at 7.40 am GMT. Stay tuned as a very exciting session of play is on your way.

The day started with Taskin Ahmed getting rid of Abdullah Shafique in the first over itself, putting Pakistan on the backfoot straight away. It was then a combination of beautiful cricket shots and good running between the wickets that helped both the batters to get their team back in the game. Shan Masood was the first to bring up his half century and his partner, Saim Ayub will be eager to get back after Lunch to get to the second half century of his Test career. Pakistan will be hoping that this partnership grows well and gets them to a good first innings total on this wicket. Bangladesh, on the other hand, will be a little disappointed with their bowling as the conditions were helpful for the fast bowlers at the start but they could only manage one wicket in the session. They need to regroup as a team and get their plans right to pick up quick wickets and get a grip back on the game.

That is the end of the first session on Day 2 of this Test match after Day 1 being washed out completely. Pakistan after being asked to bat first on a challenging wicket have batted well and currently stand at 99 runs with the loss of 1 wicket. Their skipper Shan Masood along with the youngster Saim Ayub has put up a good partnership after being 0/1 in the first over itself. Pakistan will walk off with a lot of confidence as the players head for LUNCH.

Commentary.Commentary: Well then, we are all set for the second Test to get underway. The two umpires, Michael Gough and Richard Kettleborough walk out to the middle. The players of Bangladesh are seen in a last-minute team huddle before spreading out to their respective fielding positions. For Pakistan, Abdullah Shafique and Saim Ayub are the two openers, a typical right-hand, left-hand combination. Taskin Ahmed has the new shining cherry and will straightaway bowl the first over for Bangladesh. And, here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Nick Compton is near the deck. He starts by appreciating the excellent work done by the ground staff to get the outfield and the playing surface ready for play. He mentions that while the surface has a lot of grass on it, it's important not to be deceived by its appearance. Compton shares that in the first Test, the sun baked the wicket into a batting paradise, and he expects something similar this time around. However, he does believe that the ball might offer a bit more movement early on.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Shadman Islam, Zakir Hasan, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Mominul Haque, Mushfiqur Rahim, Litton Das (WK), Shakib Al Hasan, Mehidy Hasan, Hasan Mahmud, Nahid Rana, Taskin Ahmed (In for Shoriful Islam).

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Abdullah Shafique, Saim Ayub, Shan Masood (C), Babar Azam, Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Agha Salman, Mohammad Ali, Mir Hamza (In for Shaheen Afridi), Khurram Shahzad, Abrar Ahmed (In for Naseem Shah).

The skipper of Pakistan, Shan Masood says that they would have looked to bowl first well as the wicket has been under covers for long. He further adds that it's a 4-day match now and they will have to plan the match accordingly. He says that there is a bit of grass on the wicket and they will have to wait and see how it plays in the game and finishes by saying they have picked 3 fast bowlers and 2 spinners in the line up. Informs two changes, Abrar Ahmed and Mir Hamza come in for Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah.

The captain of Bangladesh, Najmul Hossain Shanto feels that there will be some moisture on the wicket and reckons that it will help their seamers. Tells that the first Test is in the past now and they want to focus on this Test and try to follow processes. Informs that Shoriful Islam misses out due to a niggle in his groin and Taskin Ahmed comes in for him.
TOSS UPDATE - The coin flip lands in the favour of Bangladesh and Najmul Hossain Shanto elects to BOWL first.

With all said and done, and the weather looking clear for a full day’s play, the fans and the players eagerly await some on-field action this time around. We have official news - Toss to take place at 4.15 am GMT with the first ball to be bowled at 4.45 am GMT and a minimum of 98 overs will be bowled today. With an extra 30 minutes to complete the allotted overs, Stumps will be at 12.15 pm GMT. An engrossing day of Test cricket is on the cards, folks. Stay tuned for the toss and the team updates.

Delving a bit into the history of Rawalpindi. Pakistan last won here back in February 2022 against South Africa. Out of 14 Test matches played here, Pakistan have won five, all while defending the target. The best result Pakistan could get from this series is a shared trophy with a win in this game. Overall, with seven more Tests remaining in their WTC 2023-25 campaign, a win would inject some confidence in the side. Meanwhile, Bangladesh will aim to execute a whitewash which they have never done in their cricketing history on Pakistani soil so far.

Bangladesh enter the match with high morale following their impressive showing in the series opener. Their squad has been bolstered by the return of key fast bowler Taskin Ahmed, who rejoins the Test side after a 14-month absence as per the on-air commentators yesterday. With Taijul Islam also in their ranks, Bangladesh boasts considerable depth in their lineup. Since the toss hasn't happened, the team's management is likely to consider the weather conditions when finalising their playing combination. Bangladesh's primary goal will be to replicate the outstanding batting and bowling performance from the first match, which proved to be pivotal in securing the victory.

Meanwhile, Pakistan's attention remains on Babar Azam, who is still searching for form. The star Pakistani batter hasn't scored a Test century since his Boxing Day performance back in 2022. Even more concerning is his inability to reach a half-century in the intervening period, with his highest score in the past two years being just 41. This prolonged run-drought has put the spotlight squarely on Babar as he seeks to rediscover his touch in the longest format of the game.

Now, drawing our attention to the match and the combinations. It is highly likely that Pakistan will be striding out with an extra spinner given how the ball gripped and turned in the first match. Abrar Ahmed is in the frontline as he could prove handy with the ball and the bat as well. Abrar, if included in the XI will play in the whites for Pakistan after almost a year or so. The left-arm pacer Mir Hamza might also be swapped in. Since the surface has been under covers, it might assist the pacers a bit more with the swing and lateral movement.

In a twist of fate, the second Test found itself relocated to Rawalpindi from Karachi National Stadium, as the latter is undergoing a facelift for next year's Champions Trophy. However, Rawalpindi's welcome has been far from dry. Rather than gentle showers, the heavens seemed to unleash their entire reservoir, drenching the ground in an unrelenting onslaught. The teams didn’t even leave their hotels and we were left even without the toss.

Hello and a very warm welcome, folks, to our coverage of Day 2 of this second and final Test match between Pakistan and Bangladesh in Rawalpindi. Unfortunately, Mother Nature had other plans, as the consistent downpour washed out the entire first day of play. The skies over Rawalpindi remained stubbornly grey. However, the forecast for Days 2 and 3 is promising, with expectations of clear skies and no rain, so we should see some action then.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that wraps up a damp and frustrating start to the Test as persistent rain and a soggy outfield resulted in the day's play being abandoned. Looking ahead, the weather forecast for Rawalpindi suggests clearer skies for Days 2 and 3, but unfortunately, rain threats loom over Days 4 and 5. Even though the opening day's play has been called off, let's hope the rain eases soon and the outfield recovers in time for a full day of action on Day 2. Given that we have lost an entire day's play, we're likely to see early starts for the remainder of the Test. See you then. Cheers!

UPDATE - 7.14 am GMT - Well, folks! We do not have a pleasing news to share. Due to a consistent downpour in Rawalpindi, and the weather conditions not looking too encouraging for the rest of the day, the play for Day 1 has been officially CALLED OFF.

UPDATE - 7.02 am GMT - Unfortunately, we don't have good news to share. The rain continues to fall relentlessly, with the playing surface and square still under covers. A couple of match officials are out in the middle with their umbrellas, inspecting the extent of the damage the soggy outfield has sustained as they walk around.

Time to check the current World Test Championship standings for these two teams. Both faced point deductions for a slow over-rate in the first Test. Pakistan, with a 6-point deduction, are now 8th with 16 points from two wins and four losses. Bangladesh, having had a 3-point deduction, are placed 7th with 21 points from two wins and three losses in five matches. Looking ahead, Bangladesh have two away series remaining - a two-match assignment against India in September and another two-match series against the West Indies later in the year. Pakistan, on the other hand, have seven Tests remaining, including a home series against England and the West Indies, as well as an away series in South Africa.

Well, back to this Test. The buzz around is that Pakistan could tweak a bit with their all-pace attack from the first Test and swap in a spinner in place of Shaheen Afridi who was kept out of the list of the 12 probables for this Test. As stated by the Pakistani Head Coach, Jason Gillespie on the eve of the second Test, Shaheen is working on his skills to be as effective as he can be, and they are looking for the best possible combination for this game. So, it is quite possible that we may see the return of Abrar Ahmed in the mix. He can not only bowl questioning spells but also hold one end with the bat as well. And considering how the ball gripped and turned in the first match, he could be a good addition to the ranks for Pakistan. But for now, we play the waiting game and hope that the rain subsides sooner. The next official update is scheduled to be at 7 am GMT.

While we wait for the rain to relent in Rawalpindi, here's a quick recap of the opening day of the second Test between England and Sri Lanka at Lord's. Sri Lanka's captain, Dhananjaya de Silva, surprisingly opted to field first under perfect morning skies. The decision raised eyebrows, but Sri Lanka managed to chip away at the wickets through the first two sessions. Amidst this, Joe Root stood solid as a rock, scoring his 33rd Test ton, equaling Sir Alastair Cook's record for the most Test hundreds by an English batter. Gus Atkinson played a key role alongside Root and then Potts, contributing to two fifty-run partnerships, as England closed the day at 358/7.

UPDATE - 4.54 am GMT - The live visuals show that the rain is still pouring down. The skies are grey and gloomy, mirroring the soggy conditions at ground level. Unfortunately, it looks like we’re in for a long wait before any action can commence.

UPDATE - 4.27 am GMT - Arghh! As we had feared, it's currently raining heavily in Rawalpindi, and the covers are firmly in place. In fact, the rain has been persistent since last night, leading to the formation of numerous puddles in the outfield. As a result, the toss has been delayed. Sikandar Bakht informs us that the forecast suggests it might stay like this all day long. All we can do right now is keep our fingers crossed for the rain to subside soon. Stick around for further updates.

The opening day of the first Test saw rain make its presence felt, and this Test could also be marked by interruptions. While Day 2 and Day 3 are expected to be clear, the other three days we might see rain. The stage is set for another captivating encounter - will Pakistan bounce back, or will Bangladesh continue to defy the odds? Stick around for the toss and team news.

Mohammad Rizwan was the standout performer with the bat for Pakistan, but if they are to level the series, senior players like Babar Azam and captain Shan Masood will need to step up. On the bowling front, Shaheen Afridi, who had a quiet outing, has been left out of the playing XII announced a day prior, with the inclusion of leggie Abrar Ahmed. Whether he makes the final cut remains to be seen. For Bangladesh, Mushfiqur Rahim led the charge with the bat, while the spin duo of Shakib Al Hasan and Mehidy Hasan wreaked havoc in the second innings to set up Bangladesh's 7th away Test win in history.

Pakistan had a promising start in the first Test, but things quickly unravelled after what then seemed to be a bold decision to declare their first innings at 448. The Bangladeshi batters piled on the runs, giving their side a 117-run lead, and then Pakistan's batting crumbled on the final day, leading to a 10-wicket defeat. The decision to go with an all-pace attack didn't go according to plan for Pakistan, while Bangladesh, having read the conditions better, found the right balance and ended up deservedly on the winning side.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks, to the opening day of the 2nd and final Test of the series between Pakistan and Bangladesh at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. After a shocking defeat in the first Test, Pakistan are in a must-win situation to salvage pride and end the series on level terms. Meanwhile, Bangladesh, riding high on confidence from their maiden Test win against Pakistan, are eyeing a historic first-ever Test series victory over their Asian rivals.
